title: The technological frontier in fall management for older adults with dementia: A scoping review of prediction, detection, and prevention systems

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《The technological frontier in fall management for older adults with dementia: A scoping review of prediction, detection, and prevention systems》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Digital technologies for fall management: Rationale for the review · sec004-p1】In response to this growing clinical challenge, gerontechnology has produced an expanding range of digital solutions designed to support fall prediction, detection, and prevention [12]. These technologies aim to promote safe and independent aging, improve quality of life, reduce caregiver burden, and alleviate pressure on healthcare systems. However, the populations most likely to benefit from these innovations often face the greatest barriers to their successful implementation. Cognitive impairment, behavioral symptoms, resistance to routine changes, and sensory sensitivities may limit sustained engagement with digital technologies, particularly wearable devices [13,14]. Consequently, technological performance demonstrated under controlled laboratory conditions may not translate into meaningful clinical benefit. Successful implementation therefore depends not only on algorithmic performance, but also on usability, acceptability, ethical deployment, and seamless integration into routine dementia care.

【Digital technologies for fall management: Rationale for the review · sec004-p3】Accordingly, this scoping review aims to map and synthesize the current evidence on digital fall management technologies for people living with dementia. Specifically, we sought to (1) characterize the existing evidence across fall prediction, detection, and prevention technologies; (2) identify methodological, technological, and implementation challenges affecting their translation into clinical practice; and (3) highlight emerging opportunities, including artificial intelligence, multimodal sensing, and user-centered design, to inform future research and technology development.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《The technological frontier in fall management for older adults with dementia: A scoping review of prediction, detection, and prevention systems》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design · sec006-p1】This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the methodological framework originally proposed by Arksey and O'Malley (2005) and the updated guidance from the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) for scoping reviews [17,18]. This review is reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), and the completed checklist is provided in Table A in S1 Appendix. Given the iterative nature of scoping reviews and the absence of a standard requirement for prospective registration, this review was not preregistered.

【Evidence gaps limiting clinical implementation · sec024-p1】Although many technologies demonstrated promising technical performance, relatively few have generated the level of evidence required for widespread clinical implementation. For a digital health intervention to become standard of care, it must demonstrate technical feasibility and meaningful improvements in patient outcomes, scalability, and economic value under real-world conditions. Our review indicates that the current evidence base falls substantially short of these requirements.

Although many technologies demonstrated promising technical performance, relatively few have generated the level of evidence required for widespread clinical implementation. For a digital health intervention to become standard of care, it must demonstrate technical feasibility and meaningful improvements in patient outcomes, scalability, and economic value under real-world conditions. Our review indicates that the current evidence base falls substantially short of these requirements.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《The technological frontier in fall management for older adults with dementia: A scoping review of prediction, detection, and prevention systems》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Technology performance · sec015-p2】Among simulation-based studies, several machine learning models achieved near-perfect performance. Ziyad and colleagues [24] reported 100% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score for fall detection using an AdaBoost ensemble classifier trained on wearable inertial sensor data. Similarly, Szántó and colleagues [23] achieved 100% accuracy when distinguishing between 35 simulated true falls and 70 false fall events using wearable sensors. Mishra and colleagues [21] likewise demonstrated high classification performance, reporting 95% accuracy with a decision tree classifier. Although these findings demonstrate the technical potential of machine learning-based fall detection, they were derived from healthy participants performing simulated falls under controlled laboratory conditions.

【Technology performance · sec015-p3】Studies involving clinically diagnosed people living with dementia reported more modest but clinically relevant performance. For fall prediction, Adeli and colleagues [26] demonstrated that ambient monitoring of gait characteristics predicted falls occurring within four weeks, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) of 0.762, sensitivity of 0.728, and specificity of 0.732. Similarly, Schwenk and colleagues (2015) [32] reported an area under curve (AUC) of 0.771 with 0.72 sensitivity and 0.76 specificity of predicting falls over a 3-month follow-up using wearable sensor-derived gait measures.

Studies involving clinically diagnosed people living with dementia reported more modest but clinically relevant performance. sections.title: 复现线索
sections.text:
《The technological frontier in fall management for older adults with dementia: A scoping review of prediction, detection, and prevention systems》：复现时可直接核对的数据、软件或实现线索。

【The human factor: Usability, acceptability, and implementation. · sec023-p1】Technical performance alone is insufficient to ensure successful implementation of fall management technologies. Rather, sustained adoption depends on whether technologies can be integrated into the daily lives of people living with dementia. Qualitative research and systematic reviews consistently reveal that devices are often designed without sufficient consideration for the lived experience of aging and dementia [34]. This review highlights that many implementation barriers arise not from algorithmic limitations but from challenges related to usability, acceptability, and long-term adherence.

【The human factor: Usability, acceptability, and implementation. · sec023-p2】Wearable technologies exemplify this disconnect between technical capability and real-world implementation. Although inertial sensor systems demonstrated promising predictive performance [21,28], their effectiveness depends on consistent use. Cognitive impairment, memory deficits, behavioral symptoms, sensory sensitivities, and reduced dexterity may all compromise adherence by making devices uncomfortable, difficult to manage or easy to forget [35]. Consequently, technologies that perform well under experimental conditions may experience substantially reduced effectiveness when deployed in routine dementia care.
